hook: China's AI cash gap, Amazon's buyout and a U.N. stalemate
open: Tonight, China's AI cash gap, a big Amazon buyout, and the U.N. stalls on killer robots.
summary: China's tech giants are doubling AI spending to $139B while their labs earn under 8% of it, Rhodium Group says.
Amazon is reportedly near a $7.5B deal for Decart, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen's top thinking mode costs far more per request.
U.N. talks ended without binding rules on autonomous weapons, and Ethan Mollick says AI still needs human expertise.

stories.headline: China's top tech firms face growing financial gap in AI build-out
stories.summary: China's biggest tech companies are set to double their AI infrastructure capital expenditure to $139bn in 2026, according to a Rhodium Group report. Revenue from their AI labs covers less than 8% of this spending, highlighting broader financing pressures alongside US chip curbs.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows that financial constraints and low lab revenues may pose a greater challenge to China's AI development than US chip export controls alone.
source_titles: Rhodium: China's biggest tech companies are set to double capex to $139B in 2026 with AI lab revenue under 8% of it, a gap that may matter more than chip curbs (New York Times)

stories.headline: Amazon close to $7.5bn acquisition of AI startup Decart
stories.summary: Amazon is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Decart for about $7.5 billion. The deal could be finalized as early as next week, aiming to boost AWS’s computing power against rivals such as Nvidia.
stories.why_it_matters: The purchase would give Amazon’s cloud unit stronger AI hardware and software capabilities, intensifying competition in the AI infrastructure market.
source_titles: Sources: Amazon is nearing a $7.5B deal to buy AI startup Decart; talks are at an advanced stage and a deal could come together as soon as next week (Financial Times)

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen cost jumps with xhigh thinking effort mode
stories.summary: Google DeepMind’s Gemini 4 Hydrogen model shows a marked cost increase when run in xhigh thinking effort mode, rising from 3.99 cents to 23.61 cents per request and using more output tokens.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers must account for higher compute costs when opting for the model’s most capable setting, affecting budgeting and pricing for AI‑driven applications.

stories.headline: UN talks fail to produce binding rules for autonomous weapons
stories.summary: UN diplomats meeting in Geneva failed to establish legally binding rules for autonomous weapons, agreeing instead to spend two more years discussing options. Major military powers including Russia, the United States, and Israel obstructed stronger measures during the weeklong conference.
stories.why_it_matters: The delay leaves a regulatory vacuum for artificial intelligence in military applications as autonomous drones and weapons are used in active conflicts.
source_titles: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules

stories.line: U.N. talks end without binding limits on autonomous weapons

stories.anchor: Now to the battlefield, where the rules aren't coming. Russia, the U.S. and Israel blocked tougher limits at the U.N. That leaves armed drones in today's wars with no binding rules.

stories.headline: Ethan Mollick: AI models cannot yet solve complex problems alone
stories.summary: Ethan Mollick stated that combining human expertise with AI enables people to accomplish remarkable tasks, as current models cannot operate independently. He noted that mathematicians solving Millennium Problems rely on human skill because models cannot yet do it all on their own.
stories.why_it_matters: This highlights the current limits of AI models, emphasizing that human expertise remains necessary to achieve major breakthroughs.
source_titles: Ethan Mollick: We really are in a (temporary?) place where a combination of expertise and being able to work with AI allows people to do incredible…

quotes.text: We really are in a (temporary?) place where a combination of expertise and being able to work with AI allows people to do incredible things. It is no coincidence that people proving Millennium Problems have all been great mathematicians, the models can't (yet) do it all on their own.
quotes.speaker: Ethan Mollick

stories.line: Ethan Mollick: AI still needs human experts for the hardest problems
stories.detail: He notes Millennium Problem proofs have all come from great mathematicians
stories.anchor: And finally, people still matter. Professor Ethan Mollick says AI plus deep expertise can do incredible things. But alone? The models can't crack the hardest problems yet.
